# Maṇisūkarajātaka (Ja 285)
**ID:** Ja 285
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Maṇisūkarajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja285
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Maṇisūkarajātaka* (Ja 285), translated as *The Boars and the Crystal Cave*, is a birth story preserved in the Pali *Jātaka* collection [SuttaCentral]. The framing narrative, delivered by the Buddha while residing at Jetavana, is set against the conspiracy surrounding the murder of the female wanderer Sundarī, in which rival ascetics attempted to frame the Buddha in a murderous sex scandal [SuttaCentral; Jerryson and Juergensmeyer 2010; Fausböll 1879]. Eugene W. Burlingame notes that the introduction to Ja 285 recounting Sundarī's murder is virtually word-for-word identical to the account in the *Dhammapada Commentary* (xxii. 1), both ultimately drawing from the *Udāna* [Burlingame 1921].
In the past narrative, the verse opens with *Dariyā sattavassāni* [Fausböll 1879]. The Bodhisatta, living as an ascetic near a crystal cave (*maṇiguhā*), observes boars trying in vain to diminish the brilliance of the crystal before they finally abandon their effort and leave; the Bodhisatta subsequently attains the Brahmā realm through the cultivation of meditative absorption (*jhāna*) [Fausböll 1879]. The Buddha concludes the teaching by identifying himself as the ascetic of that time [Fausböll 1879].
Curated records on SuttaCentral list four translations in four languages [SuttaCentral]. While no cross-language parallels with score ≥ 10 are recorded by DharmaNexus, automated text-reuse analysis shows that Ja 285 shares four passages with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), with its principal verse segment (§§1.1–2.4) matching the commentary (§§2669_9–2675) at a similarity of 0.92 [DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a2) (§1.1–2.4 ↔ §2669_9–2675)

- [SuttaCentral] SuttaCentral entry for ja285 — Supplied canonical metadata, English title, blurb, and translation counts.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database (ja285) — Provided automated internal Pali text reuse matches with the Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā.
- [Burlingame 1921] Eugene Watson Burlingame, Buddhist Legends: Translated from the Original Pali Text of the Dhammapada Commentary (1921) — Noted the derivation of the introductory story of Sundarī from the Udāna and its correspondence with DhpA xxii. 1.
- [Jerryson and Juergensmeyer 2010] Michael Jerryson and Mark Juergensmeyer, eds., Buddhist Warfare (2010) — Discussed the frame story as depicting a conspiracy to implicate the Buddha in a murderous sex scandal.
